newsitem.title: GERMANY: Europe imported shoe prices to double-Deichmann.
newsitem.headline: Europe imported shoe prices to double-Deichmann.

text.p: German retailer Deichmann Schuhe GmbH & Co on Monday warned the cost of cheap shoes would double if the EU goes ahead with plans to slap an anti dumping duty on footwear imported from Thailand, Indonesia and China.

Heinrich Deichmann, managing partner of Europe's leading footwear specialist, said in a telephone interview that European firms would be forced to seek new markets for products such as China's rubberised canvas shoes if the duty is imposed.

"This measure will have an extraordinarily bad effect on the shoe market," he said, noting that such footwear was no longer produced in any European country and that there was no evidence that the cheap imports had damaged retailers here.

He added that it was very doubtful the duty would be supported by the European shoe industry in general and that Deichmann and a group of other retailers planned to take legal action if the EU proceeds to impose it.
While the European Union has not yet taken a final decision to levy the duty, Deichmann said it would "in all probability" do so.
Deichmann, whose Essen-based firm has over 2.8 billion marks in annual sales, said imports from Thailand, Indonesia and China accounted for 50 percent of the low-cost canvas shoes sold in Europe.
The duty would add 94 percent to the cost of Chinese imports and mean slightly lower increases in the other two countries.
